sessions.title: Catalunya 2030: A €1 Billion Bet on AI
sessions.speakers: Albert Tort Pugibet, Maria Galindo Garcia-Delgado
sessions.brief: In this session, Albert Tort, Secretary of Telecommunications and Digital Transformation of the Generalitat de Catalunya, and Maria Galindo, Secretary for Digital Policies of the Government of Catalonia, will explain Catalunya's plan to invest €1 billion in artificial intelligence by 2030 — and what it means for...

sessions.title: Forward Deployment at OpenAI
sessions.brief: A look inside a Forward Deployed Engineering project building a tax AI system, where production traces become evaluations and coding agents turn observed failures into tested improvements.

sessions.title: Beyond the Pilot: Making Enterprise AI Pay Off
sessions.brief: 79% of enterprises struggle to turn AI investment into value — yet the winners report 5-10x returns. Leaders from global enterprises on what separates pilots that die from AI that pays.

sessions.title: The Hidden Blockers to Autonomous Operations
sessions.brief: Autonomous AI agents promise to revolutionize enterprise operations, moving beyond simple chat interfaces to execute complex, multi-step business workflows. Yet, despite massive investments in state-of-the-art LLMs, most enterprise agent pilots hit a hard wall when deployed into real-world operational environments.

sessions.title: Hacking and Cybersecurity in the age of AI
sessions.brief: AI has changed dramatically many areas. Cybersecurity is one of them. Searching, exploiting and patching vulns or managing cybersecurity is completely related to AI, but at the same time AI Digital Services and Agentic AI are bringing new set of vulnerabilities, therefore exploiting AI and securing AI is a new task...

sessions.title: When code is cheap, governance is the hard part
sessions.brief: The Challenge Code generation is close to free now. Review, sign-off, and audit are not, and that gap lands squarely on engineering leaders. In this session, I'll show you where AI-generated changes actually fail before production, and how automated checks and audit trails hold humans and AI to the same standard...

sessions.title: The Ultra-Scale Talk: Scaling Training to Thousands of GPUs
sessions.brief: Training large language models demands more than raw compute. it requires a deep understanding of parallelism and architecture choices. This talk dives into the practicalities of ultra-scale training: how 5D parallelism makes it possible to stretch a single run across massive GPU clusters, how Mixture-of-Experts...

sessions.title: Fireside Chat: Applied AI in Practice: Anthropic’s Plans for Spain
sessions.brief: Fireside chat with Julia Hernandez, Member of Technical Staff, Applied AI, Spain at Anthropic. A conversation about deploying Claude in businesses and Anthropic’s plans for the Spanish AI ecosystem.

sessions.title: Gen AI: Myths and Reality
sessions.brief: Despite what you might think from reading the news since late 2022, Artificial Intelligence did not appear with ChatGPT. This "Revolution" is merely the fruit of a long maturation, spanning several decades. After a brief historical review, we'll delve into these new AIs, the Generative AIs.

sessions.title: Satellites, Planes, Trains: Why Hardware's Cursor Moment Just Started
sessions.brief: Claude and Cursor are already transforming how software is written: accelerating development, augmenting engineers, and collapsing the gap between idea and implementation. Hardware is next.

sessions.title: Moving beyond Productivity: How Enterprise AI Creates Organizational Impact at Scale
sessions.brief: AI is taking hold in the enterprise — and yet many organizations are still waiting for the payoff. The tools are powerful. The potential is real. But something fundamental is missing between individual productivity and lasting organizational impact.

sessions.title: Fireside Chat with BlackRock
sessions.brief: Martin C. Syms, Managing Director and International Head of BlackRock's Aladdin Engineering Group, in conversation with Cathy White on where AI actually creates value in finance. Trusted data as the foundation of sustainable AI business models.

sessions.title: Rebuilding the Org Chart: What Actually Breaks When Enterprises Restructure Around AI
sessions.brief: Every enterprise AI rollout eventually stops being a technology project and becomes an org design problem. Job descriptions written for execution, teams built around headcount, managers measured on output that agents now produce.

sessions.title: The art of the possible: Agentic AI, by Google Cloud
sessions.brief: Concrete case studies highlighting what is viable today versus what is emerging over the next 12–18 months.

sessions.title: DXC CoreIQ: Applying AI to Mainframe Legacy at Massive Scale
sessions.brief: Mainframes still run the world's critical transaction systems, but the COBOL and assembler underneath are becoming lost knowledge. DXC CoreIQ turns a multi-million-line legacy codebase into a live knowledge base — continuously updated code-understanding graphs navigated by AI agents, with every answer traceable back...

sessions.brief: Everyone's talking about voice AI. In this room, you'll actually ship one. Roshan and Barbara will get you from a blank screen to a working, talking AI agent that can hold a real phone conversation, before the coffee break ends.

sessions.title: The AI Advantage Isn’t Individual: Why the biggest gains will come from rethinking how teams work together.
sessions.brief: AI has transformed what one person can do. But building great products has always been a team sport. In this talk, Rory Keddie from Miro explores how product teams are adapting - moving from fragmented AI usage to collaborative, agent-powered workflows.

sessions.title: Debate 3 — Sovereign AI or Surrender? Should Europe Stop Outsourcing Its AI Future?
sessions.brief: Europe is building 13 AI Factories, funding Mistral and Aleph Alpha, demanding open weights, and writing the world's strictest AI law. Yet 90% of European AI compute still runs on AWS, Azure and GCP, and the foundation model leaderboards are American and Chinese.

sessions.title: Money, Reinvented: AI Agents, Stablecoins & the Future of Finance
sessions.brief: Agents that pay, tokenized rails, banks racing fintechs to deploy AI under the world's strictest rules. The people building the future of money on what's real and what's next.

sessions.title: Your User Is Asleep at 3am. What Is Your Agent Allowed to Do?
sessions.brief: Almost every agent at this conference assumes there's someone there to answer it. Ours often can't be: the traveller is in the air, asleep, or standing at a gate at three in the morning. That changes what you have to build. A booking isn't a transaction — it's a workflow that can break for weeks.

sessions.title: Deploying AI Across the Workforce with Gemini Enterprise, by Google Cloud
sessions.brief: Move beyond passive search and rigid assistants. In this session, you will discover how any employee can build custom AI agents, automate workflows across your existing stack, and establish the governance layer needed to scale securely across the organization with Gemini Enterprise

sessions.title: Leverage AI to Build MVPs fast
sessions.brief: Compress your time-to-market by building and shipping functional MVPs in days using AI coding assistants, code generation, and rapid prototyping pipelines. Focus on validating demand early and iterating fast while adopting AI-native execution to automate development workflows and significantly increase output.

sessions.title: Greener AI is possible: the decisions behind Ecosia's AI products
sessions.brief: Ecosia is a search engine owned by a foundation. It can't be sold, it will never go public, and 100% of its profits go to climate action. We built generative AI without pretending the costs weren't real but knowing Greener AI was not impossible.

sessions.title: AI for data analytics
sessions.brief: In this session we will cover how the data analytics has been impacted by AI and get a glimpse of a possible future in agentic analytics.

sessions.title: Who's Really Deciding? Human Agency in the Age of AI
sessions.brief: An algorithm nudges what your kid reads before bed. A hiring filter decides who a recruiter never sees. A health app flags what's wrong before your doctor does. None of this is speculative — it's this year's default UX.

sessions.title: The AI Enterprise Value Gap
sessions.brief: AI capabilities are growing at an unprecedented pace, with a never ending flow of new models that beat every single benchmark. However, enterprise value barely reflects this, and most AI initiatives fail to reach production and provide measurable impact, generating a gap between the technological capabilities...

sessions.title: AEO (Answer Engine Optimization): The Critical Growth Channel
sessions.brief: AI Visibility (appearing in AI recommendations) is imperative amidst the current decline in search traffic. Understand the nature of the moment and what you can do to take advantage of it.

sessions.title: Tokens, Latency, Sovereignty: The Physics Pulling AI to the Edge
Dataiku
sessions.brief: To be announced...

sessions.title: Cybercoding in Live Action: Securing a Legacy Application
sessions.brief: Modernizing Enterprise Software: The Cybercoding Methodology In an era defined by accelerating cyber threats and stringent European regulatory demands—specifically NIS2 compliance for all B2B SaaS platforms—traditional application refactoring is no longer viable.

sessions.title: "Who Owns What AI Made? A Practical Framework for IP, Compliance, and Trust in AI-Driven Creative Work"
sessions.brief: Every AI-generated asset your team produces today carries a question nobody wants to answer under deadline pressure: Who owns it? What does the EU AI Act require? And did the tool you used just quietly claim rights to your client's brief? This talk cuts through the ambiguity.

sessions.title: Not your weights, not your brain!
sessions.brief: Can open models drive your agentic needs? This session explores the current state of open AI, including local AI. It then goes on to examine how to incorporate open models to your workflow. Open models come in many flavors and sizes: from large near-frontier behemoth models, to small models that can run on your laptop.

sessions.title: Memory in AI systems - Why state is the missing keystone
sessions.brief: When your agent decides something is worth remembering past its current session, where does that write go today, and how is it retrieved? We will discuss how data layers and agent state memory are critical to scalable, productionised agentic workflows.

sessions.title: AI at Damm: Real-World Use Cases from a 150-Year-Old Company
The New Gatekeepers: Brand Visibility in the Age of AI Search
sessions.brief: Zero-click search is here: customers ask AI, not Google. How GEO is replacing SEO, what happens to your website when agents do the browsing, and who wins when LLMs decide what gets seen.

sessions.title: Shifting Gears: A Practical Guide to Adopting Spec-Driven Development
sessions.brief: As AI coding agents become mainstream, engineering teams are discovering a new problem: freestyle AI generates code without traceability. When the AI writes the code directly from a prompt, how do you answer, "Why was this built this way?" In this session, we will explore Nuvolar's pragmatic journey to Spec-Driven...

sessions.title: Orbio
The Wrong Question: Why Human-in-the-Loop Is No Longer Enough
sessions.brief: Human-in-the-Loop has become a technical checkbox: a person somewhere in the pipeline, approving outputs. Alia Zafar argues that is the wrong question. The decisions that determine how AI reshapes work, inequality, climate and national competitiveness are not made in the loop.

sessions.title: From Wrong Parts to Right Revenue: AI-Driven Spare Parts Identification in Manufacturing
sessions.brief: To be announced...

sessions.title: The AI Founder's Diary: 16 Months of Building AI-First Companies
sessions.brief: Vincent Jong has spent the last 16 months testing whether one person can build a real company with AI. The result: three products launched solo. One is flat, one is growing, one one he shut down. In this session he walks through what actually happened.

sessions.title: Your AI Can Write the UI. This Makes Sure It Writes Your UI.
sessions.brief: AI agents build UI by imitating what already exists in your codebase. If your repo holds design debt, your AI will multiply it. Learn how npx roast-my-design-system, an open-source deterministic auditor and MCP server, measures system health, generates ready-to-run fix prompts for instant cleanup, precise agent rules...

sessions.title: AI vs AI: Deepfakes, Detection & the Trust Gap
sessions.brief: Deepfakes and automated attacks are getting cheaper faster than defences are catching up. What detection can actually catch today, what it takes to prove an AI system can be trusted, and how far a supervisory authority can reach. Fighting AI with AI, from the detection lab to the audit. +1

sessions.title: When we crashed our AI Interviewer and Amplitude saved our lives
BizAway Lab: Harness Building: Build a full-featured travel app with us
sessions.brief: We’re handing you the keys to a working BizAway travel client, and the harness to build on top of it. Login is ready to go; everything after that is a sandbox designed for you to extend, automate, and customize.

sessions.title: Futures workshop. Coming of Age 20/40
sessions.brief: Coming of Age 20/40 invites you to an exploration of the future and challenge your thinking to go beyond the current mode of using AI. You will meet four young Europeans from 2040 — Rowan, Nova, Cypher and Zane.

sessions.title: Why most AI GTM fails (and what's converting instead)
sessions.brief: Many AI products impress in demos but stall in adoption. This talk explores the gap between technical possibility and commercial traction: the buyer signals that matter, the pricing and positioning shifts that unlock budget, and the product traps that quietly kill deals.

sessions.title: Future of healthcare AI
sessions.brief: Matěj Misař is one of the leading voices driving the real-world implementation of artificial intelligence in healthcare across Central and Eastern Europe. While many still view CEE as a “catch-up region,” the reality may surprise you.

sessions.title: The Real Disruption isn't AI. It is Human Intelligence.
sessions.brief: AI is changing how organisations work, but the deeper shift is human. Myriam Ben Farhat, VP of People Experience & Inclusion at Chess.com, on why human and emotional intelligence, leadership and organisational culture decide whether AI transformation actually works, and what that asks of the people leading it.

sessions.title: Data, Context, and Intelligence: How Uberall Built an Agentic Planning Architecture with Pigment
sessions.brief: Join Anselme Vignon (Pigment) and Jose Ramon Iglesias (Uberall) to discover how Uberall transformed its FP&A processes using Agentic AI. This session explores the winning formula of "Data + Context + Intelligence," revealing how Uberall solved the missing piece of the AI puzzle to achieve over 95% accuracy in their...

sessions.title: How to reach 10M€ ARR in 5 years self funded with a family business ?
sessions.brief: Leexi was founded in late 2021 by Xavier Lombard, his wife and two sons, born from a simple frustration: the value created in professional meetings disappears without a trace.

sessions.title: Panel 18 — BlueTechPort: Shaping Responsible AI for the Blue Economy
sessions.brief: AI needs more than algorithms and computing power. It depends on physical infrastructure — energy, water, data centres and connectivity — but also on governance infrastructure: regulation, institutions, trust and the right market incentives.

sessions.title: Everyone Is 10x. The Company Isn't.
sessions.brief: A year ago, getting developers to use AI was the hard part. It isn't anymore. Give them agents, and they'll use them: three to five each, chosen per task, every choice defensible on its own. What breaks now is everything around them. Knowledge stays trapped in whichever tool produced it.

sessions.title: Experiencing the Spanish AI Act Sandbox
sessions.brief: We’ll be sharing InfoJobs’ lessons learned from participating in the Spanish AI Act Sandbox. We will explain how the Sandbox was structured, look at the guidance and tools provided by the experts, and show the High Risk adaptation framework proposed during the initiative.

sessions.title: Coding with AI - The good, the bad and the ugly
sessions.brief: Everyone knows Claude Code. Codex, too. But what happens when you actually try to build with them inside a big company? That's where the difficulties appear — out of nowhere. What we learned is that two things make the difference: fundamentals, and visualization.

sessions.title: Debate 4 — The 2027 Crash: Is AI the New Dot-Com Bubble?
sessions.brief: $500 billion in AI capex this year alone. NVIDIA at a $4-trillion market cap. Startups raising $1 billion before product. And a chorus of investors, economists and former bulls now whispering the b-word.

sessions.title: From BSC to Brussels: Europe's Supercomputing Bet on AI
sessions.brief: Frontier AI runs on supercomputers — and right now, Europe is on a building spree. The AI Factories initiative is wiring 13 supercomputers across the continent. Barcelona's MareNostrum 5 already sits in the global top tier.

sessions.title: How to write a rubric properly
sessions.brief: In this workshop, you will learn how to evaluate frontier AI Models. You will create a checklist and have others score a model according to yours. You will learn the properties that separate a real rubric from a plausible ones, and how to balance between difficulty and plausibility.

sessions.title: Conforama
sessions.brief: To be announced...

sessions.title: Workshop 19
Automated, Augmented or Resilient? A Live AI Task Audit
sessions.brief: AI doesn't replace jobs in one go. It takes over tasks, one by one. In Europe, 53% of jobs are already exposed to AI, and many will transform. The most useful way to see where your job is heading is to look at what actually fills your week, not your job title.

sessions.title: Fair, Explainable, Accountable: Building Responsible AI in Production
sessions.brief: Every company claims their AI is responsible — few can show the audit trail. Bias testing that catches real bias, explainability that survives a regulator's questions, and the governance structures that hold up when a customer, a journalist, or a lawsuit comes asking.

sessions.title: Use Case 15
Fireside 7 — How a Mortgage Broker Becomes an AI Company
sessions.speakers: Ricard Garriga, Josep Maria Ribes Bonet
sessions.brief: What happens when artificial intelligence moves from being a supporting technology to becoming a core part of a company’s value proposition? This fireside chat will explore how AI is reshaping the mortgage and real estate sector through the experience of a company undergoing that transformation firsthand.

sessions.title: The Best AI Opportunities Might Be in the Industries Nobody Wants to Build For.
sessions.brief: What if the biggest AI opportunities aren’t in the most crowded markets, but in the industries technology has overlooked for years? We’ll share how we went from building AI automations for property management companies to uncovering deeper pain points in a sector still heavily reliant on legacy software, fragmented...

sessions.title: Everyone Talks AI. Who’s Actually Transforming?
sessions.brief: AI pilots are everywhere. Real transformation is harder to find. In this fireside chat, Enric Escalé Garrell, Partner at SDG Group, cuts through the AI hype to explore what separates experimentation from meaningful business transformation.

sessions.title: AI Visibility: How Buyers Find You Without Searching
sessions.brief: AI is changing how people discover and choose products. This panel breaks down how tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews decide what to recommend and how brands can actually show up there. Expect practical strategies around content, brand mentions, and distribution that drive pipeline.

sessions.title: Beyond the bot ... what makes a voice agent worth talking to
sessions.brief: Most voice agents are built to be useful. Very few are built to be good to talk to. There's a difference and it matters more than we think. In this talk, we map the spectrum of what AI voice conversations can actually be.

sessions.title: Barcelona: A Place Where Innovation Flourishes
sessions.brief: Barcelona is not just a city — it is a European innovation hub with a strategy. The BlueTechPort brings together the city's Blue Economy ambitions, startup energy, and institutional backing into one living ecosystem.

sessions.title: Closing ceremony by the Molt Honorable Mr. Salvador Illa i Roca, President of the Government of Catalonia.
sessions.brief: Salvador Illa i Roca This agenda covers the two summit days. AI Week starts earlier — including the hackathon weekend on 19–20 September, and the side events across the city. Want to be in these sessions? Two days, seven tracks, 200+ speakers at WTC Barcelona.
